title: Inheritance and inherited properties
learningObjectives: Distinguish inherited CSS properties from non-inherited properties and use inheritance intentionally.

understand.concept: Inheritance is the process by which some CSS properties pass from a parent element to its descendants when the child has no winning declaration of its own.
understand.whyItMatters: It reduces repeated rules. Text-related properties such as color and font-family commonly inherit, while layout properties such as margin, padding and border do not normally inherit.
understand.analogy: A parent can pass some shared settings, such as the preferred text style, to children.
understand.analogyLimit: CSS inheritance is property-specific. Children do not automatically copy every visual or layout setting from a parent.

explain.narrative: Set color and font-family on the body and the paragraph and link inside it normally receive those values. A margin on the body does not become the paragraph's margin through inheritance. A child declaration can override an inherited value. Use browser developer tools to inspect computed values and identify whether a value is inherited.

examples.explanation: The body sets a dark text colour and a system font. The paragraph inherits both. The .special rule overrides only the paragraph colour.
examples.expectedOutput: The element appears according to the winning CSS rule described in the explanation.

practise.guidedTask: Remove color from .special and observe inheritance. Then add padding to body and check whether the paragraph receives the same padding as its own computed value.
practise.independentTask: Create a parent section with inherited text styles and a child heading that overrides one property. Explain which values inherit and which do not.
hints: Inheritance is not the same as the cascade.
Check the specific property's inheritance behaviour.
